 *******
 Judgment

Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.18,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of Lorry bearing No.KA-25-B-8666, alleging that on 05.02.2022 at 02.30 a.m., when traveling by sitting in a Car bearing No.KA-05-ML-9294 on NH-48, near Shamnur Bridge, within the limits of Davanagere South Traffic Police Station, driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-25-B-8666 negligently parked the same on the middle of the road, thereby made the Car to dash to the rear part of the Lorry bearing No.KA-25-B-8666, thereby became the reason for the accident, resulting in injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Government Hospital, Davanagere, BGS Global Hospital, Kengeri.
3. Regarding the accident Davanagere South Traffic police registered a case in Crime No.15/2022.
4. As on the date of accident, petitioner being aged 23 years, used to earn Rs.14,402/- p.m., by working as Junior Relationship Executive at Muthoot Finance Limited.
5. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 owner of the Lorry remained absent.

6. In response to the notice, respondent No.2 - Insurance Company appeared through his advocate,
filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

7. On the basis of the pleadings on 17.12.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 05.02.2022 at about 02.30 a.m., on Chitradurga - Davanagere NH-48, near Davanagere Taluk, in view of the negligent parking of a Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-25-B- 8666, Mahindra Car bearing Reg. No.KA-05- ML-9294 dashed to the rear part of the Lorry, thereby accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner, one of the inmate of the Car?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
8. On 03.02.2023, 28.08.2024 and 25.03.2025 petitioner deposed as P.W.1 and produced 20 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.19 and Ex.P.31.

On 04.10.2023 and 07.02.2024 petitioner produced the evidence of Head Constable, South Traffic Police Station, Davanagere and MRO, BGS Hospital,
Kengeri as P.W.2 and 3 and get produced 11 documents at Exs.P.20 to 30.
Gautham.

2 9.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of respondent No.2-Insurance company and perused the records.

10. On the basis of the material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...

Due to the negligent use of the Car bearing No.KA-05-ML-9294 and Lorry bearing No.KA-25-B-8666 at the ratio of 50:50, collusion taken place between the front part of Car and rear part of the Lorry resulting in the injuries to the petitioner.
Issue No.2 ...
Petitioner is entitle to receive  Rs.1,24,992/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 11. Issue No.1:

In the evidence petitioner stated that on 05.02.2022 at 02.30 a.m.,
when traveling by sitting in a Car bearing No.KA-05-ML-9294 on NH-48, near Shamnur Bridge, Davanagere, driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-25- B-8666 negligently parked the same on the middle of the highway, thereby made the Car to hit to the rear part of the Lorry bearing No.KA-25-B-8666, thereby became the reason for the accident,
resulting in injuries to him and other inmates of the car.
12. In the written statement respondent No.2 Insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.

13. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 submitted that during accident, he was sitting on the front left seat of the car and immediately prior to the accident, head light of the car was in proper condition.
P.W.1 stated that he saw the stationary Lorry on Bengaluru - Davanagere NH-48.

Petitioner denied the suggestion that at 02.30 a.m., his friend Vishwanath negligently under drowsiness drove the car,
dashed the same to rear part of the stationary Lorry.

14. In the evidence P.W.2 Head Constable of South Traffic Police Station, Davanagere produced copy of the Insurance Policy of the Lorry, copies of registration certificate, 'B' register extract,
permit, Fitness Certificate and Driving Licence of driver of the Lorry at Exs.P.20 to P.25.
Gautham.N vs Ningappa Kurubar on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76856357/
3 15.

In the evidence MRO of BGS Hospital, Kengeri produced MLC Register extract at Ex.P.29.
16.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR with complaint pertaining to crime No.15/2022 registered by Davanagere South Traffic police on 05.02.2022 against Basavaraj Tadasad driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-25-B-8666 for having committed offence punishable under Sections 283, 337 of IPC,
on the basis of the complaint presented by Nagaraja B.A., S/o.Ashwat Narayana, one of the inmate of the car.
Ex.P.3 is the copy Wound Certificate, issued by SSIMS & RC Hospital, Davanagere, in which reason for the injuries are noted as, 'RTA near Bathi, Davanagere at 2.30 a.m. on 05.02.2022'.

Ex.P.31 is the copy of charge sheet with enclosures, which shows that after investigation,
Davanagere South Traffic police in Cr.No.15/2022 filed charge sheet against Basavaraj Thadasad S/o.Malappa Tadasad, driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-25-B-8666 for having committed offence punishable under Sections 283, 337, 338 of IPC and Section 3(1), 181 of IMV Act.
17. In this case evidence of driver of the Car and driver of the Lorry are not available.
18. As referred above, in the evidence P.W.1 submitted that immediately prior to the accident, he noticed stationary Lorry.
19. In this case there is no explanation on behalf of petitioner for what reason the Car was dashed to the rear part of Lorry on the national highway.

20. Hence, I have concluded that on 05.02.2022 at 02.30 a.m., on NH-48, near Shamnur Bridge,
within the limits of Davanagere South Traffic Police Station, due to the negligent use of Car bearing No.KA-05-ML-9294 by Vishwanath and negligent use of Lorry bearing No.KA-25- B-8666 by Basavaraj Tadasad at the ratio of 50:50, collusion taken place between front part of the Car and rear part of the Lorry, resulting in injuries to the petitioner, one of the inmates of the car.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 accordingly.
21. Issue No.2:

In the evidence P.W.1 stated that in the accident he has suffered fracture of femur and other injuries, took first aid at Government Hospital, Davanagere, then at took treatment at BGS Global Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 05.02.2022 to 15.02.2022, underwent surgery by spending Rs.3,00,000/- and requires to take further treatment at the cost of Rs.1,00,000/-.
P.W.1 stated that as on the date of incident used to earn Rs.15,000/- p.m. by working as Mechanic.
22. In the written statement, respondent No.2 - Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

23. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of cross-examination,
he do not require to take further treatment at a cost of Rs.1,00,000/-.
P.W.1 denied the suggestion that he never spent Rs.4,80,000/- for treatment, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges.

P.W.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident, he neither worked as a Mechanic/Junior Executrive at Muthoot Finance, nor earned Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Gautham.N vs Ningappa Kurubar on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76856357/
4 24.
In the evidence P.W.2 - Head Constable, South Traffic police stated nothing regarding nature and consequence of injuries suffered by the petitioner.

25. In the evidence P.W.3-MRO of BGS Hospital, Kengeri produced OP Card, Inpatient record, copy of MLC register extract and X-rays at Exs.P.26 to P.30.
26.

Wound certificate, OPD Slips, Medical certificates, case file, X-rays and other medical records shows that in the accident petitioner suffered fracture of right femur, took treatment at SSIMS Hospital, Davanagere, BGS Global Hospital, Kengeri as an inpatient from 05.02.2022 to 15.02.2022.
In the medical records, age of the petitioner is noted as 23 years as on the date of incident.
Medical bills shows that petitioner spent approximately Rs.35,984/- for treatment.
In this case petitioner has not produced documentary evidence regarding his occupation and quantum of his income.
27. In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding nature of injury suffered, length, place and nature of treatment taken by the petitioner.

Hence, I assess compensation at Rs.65,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.35,984/- towards treatment charges, Rs.15,000/- towards conveyance, attendant and nourishment charges, Rs.84,000/-
(Rs.14,000/- x 6) towards loss of income during treatment period, Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.
28.

Hence, I assess total compensation at Rs.2,49,984/-.
29.
In view of the findings recorded on Issue No.1, petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.1,24,992/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.

Sl. No. Heads of Compensation Amount Rs.
1) Pain and agony 65,000.00 2) Treatment charges 35,984.00 3) Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000.00  attendant charges 4) Loss of income during treatment 84,000.00  period (Rs.14,000/- x 6)
5) Loss of amenities and future 50,000.00

unhappiness:
 Total: 2,49,984.00
Less: 50% negligence attributed by the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-ML-9294: 1,24,992.00

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly.
Gautham.N vs Ningappa Kurubar on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76856357/
5 30.
Issue No.3:
In para No.9 of the written statement respondent No.2 - Insurance company admitted the subsistence of policy with respect to the Lorry bearing No.KA-25-B-8666 as on the date of incident.
Copy of the policy marked at Ex.P.20 shows that as on the date of incident, Lorry had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.

Documents marked at Ex.P.22 to P.24 shows that as on the date of incident, Lorry bearing No.KA-25-B-8666 had permit and F.C. Copy of Driving License marked at Ex.P.25 shows that since 03.08.2001 to 02.08.2021 Basavaraj Tadasad had license to drive non-transport vehicles, since 19.02.2008 to 29.07.2021 Basavaraj Tadasad had license to drive transport vehicles i.e. subsequent to 29.07.2021 Basavaraj Tadasad has not get renewed his driving license.

However, non-renewal of driving license alone is not sufficient to exonerate the Insurance Company to deposit compensation payable to the petitioner, who is a third party, reserving liberty to recover so deposited money from respondent No.1.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the Lorry bearing No.KA-25-B-8666 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.1,24,992/- (Rupees One Lakh Twenty Four thousand Nine hundred and Ninety Two only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.

The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Lorry bearing No.KA-25-B-8666 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today,
reserving liberty to recover so deposited money from respondent No.1 by taking steps in accordance with law, if interested.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 6th day of May, 2025.)

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
